newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits fatten in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits fatten in second quarter.

text.p: Profits of U.S. manufacturing companies rose briskly in the second quarter as sales strengthened in an expanding economy, the Commerce Department said Friday.
A quarterly survey of about 7,900 companies showed that after-tax profits climbed rose to a seasonally adjusted 6.2 cents per dollar of sales from 5.8 cents in the first quarter last year.
The improvement occurred as the economy grew at its strongest quarterly rate in two years, with the nation's gross domestic product booming ahead at a 4.8 percent annual rate between April and June.

Manufacturers' profits after taxes during the second quarter totalled a seasonally adjusted $57 billion on net sales of $918.7 billion. That was 8 percent higher than the first quarter's profits of $52.8 billion on net sales of $906.8 billion.
Manufacturing companies did much better in the second quarter this year than during the comparable three-month period in 1995.
Profits this year were 11 percent higher than in the second quarter of 1995, when manufacturers' after-tax earnings were $51.4 billion on net sales of $869.8 billion.

Producers of both long-lasting durable goods, like cars and refrigerators, and nondurable goods, like quickly used food and paper products, had fatter earnings in the second quarter than they did in the opening three months of the year.
Durables producers' profits after taxes were up to a seasonally adjusted $26.6 billion from $24.4 billion in the first quarter.
Companies that make nondurable goods like paper and food products had higher profits of $30.4 billion in the second quarter, compared with $28.4 billion in the first quarter of this year.
